note: Clinker burning in large preheater-precalciner kilns with fourth-generation clinker coolers (state of the art, cooler efficiency about 75% of the theoretical maximum) and burners designed for high alternative-fuel co-incineration; overall thermal process efficiency above 80% of the theoretical maximum.
Maximum clinker output of the largest kilns "now lies between 12,000 and 13,000 tpd"; an upper size bound, not a typical unit size. CAPACITY BASIS: product-output (clinker).

Waste heat recovery generating electricity from clinker-burning exhaust and cooler air; conventional water-steam cycles operate from heat-source temperatures as low as 300 degC, ORC and Kalina cycles below that.

Commercial: 525 cement-plant installations in 2009 and 865 by 2012, more than 95% in Asia (85% in China); conventional steam technology 99% of installed WHR systems, only nine ORC and two Kalina systems installed. reprinted from IFC/IIP (2014) and Harder (2013).
Post-combustion CO2 capture as an end-of-pipe solution on the kiln exhaust: chemical absorption, adsorption, membranes, mineralisation or calcium looping.

Pilot plants (Brevik, Skyonic, Taiwan Cement); discussed as a potential capture method for short-term implementation in 2020. Fig. 11 direct CO2 avoidance costs are bars without printed values (see other-values).

Kiln fired with oxygen and recirculated flue gas (mainly CO2) as secondary air; the recirculation rate strongly affects thermal energy demand; clinker of the same quality can be produced under a CO2/O2 atmosphere.
Basic research; detailed R&D needed before pilot scale; ECRA preparing a concept study for an oxyfuel pilot kiln; one producer planning a pilot test in France.
"a commercial application is not expected before 2030"; loaded as the earliest year (value-min).
Vertical roller mills: predominant for raw-material grinding and well established for cement finish grinding; most new equipment concepts focus on VRMs and their drives.
Commercial; 113 VRMs ordered for new installations worldwide (excluding China) in 2012, versus 51 ball mills and 27 HPGR. reprinted from Harder (2013).
High-pressure grinding rolls (roller presses), often in conjunction with ball mills; over 60% of Chinese cement is produced on grinding systems with HPGRs.
Commercial; 27 new orders outside China in 2012; dominant in China. reprinted from Harder (2013) and Wei et al. (2013).

Ball mills: reliable and easy to operate for cement grinding, still widely used in existing and new grinding units, but energy efficiency remains a challenge; optimisation of ball charges reveals large savings potential.
Commercial; 51 ordered outside China in 2012.
Ternary cements (CEM II/C-M and CEM VI to EN 197-1) with reduced clinker content using fly ash, slag, limestone, pozzolana or calcined clay as main constituents.
Shortly to be standardised in Europe; broad application seems possible in the near future.
Belite-rich clinker burned like OPC clinker but at lower temperatures of around 1250-1300 degC.
Sulphoaluminate clinker, main phase ye'elimite (C4A3s), requiring a burning temperature of about 1250 degC and easy to grind.
Belite-calciumsulfoaluminate-ternesite (BCT) clinker combining CSA and belite cement properties.
"CO2 emissions of BCT clinker are around 30% lower than those from conventional OPC" (per t clinker). reprinted from Dienemann et al. (2013).
Produced on a semi-industrial scale; up-scaling to industrial dimensions planned.
CELITEMENT: calcium and silica starting materials, hydrothermal autoclave process followed by reactive grinding; no rotary kiln.
Pilot research status; energy demand data not yet available; first field of application special construction materials.
